Verified filing excerpts (extractive audit evidence; no derived calculations):

- Azure faces diverse competition from companies such as Amazon, Broadcom, Google, IBM, Oracle, and open source offerings. [MSFT-2024-10K-p000023](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000095017024087843/msft-20240630.htm) (chunk: `000095017024087843#passage-000023`; accession: `0000950170-24-087843`).
- Our AI offerings compete with AI products from hyperscalers such as Amazon and Google, as well as products from other emerging competitors, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, and other open source offerings [MSFT-2024-10K-p000023](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000095017024087843/msft-20240630.htm) (chunk: `000095017024087843#passage-000023`; accession: `0000950170-24-087843`).
- A material part of our business involves cloud-based services available across the spectrum of computing devices. Our competitors continue to develop and deploy cloud-based services for consumers and business customers, and pricing and delivery models are evolving. [MSFT-2024-10K-p000046](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000095017024087843/msft-20240630.htm) (chunk: `000095017024087843#passage-000046`; accession: `0000950170-24-087843`).
- We will bear significant development and operational costs to build and support the AI models, services, platforms, and infrastructure necessary to meet the needs of our customers. [MSFT-2024-10K-p000046](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000095017024087843/msft-20240630.htm) (chunk: `000095017024087843#passage-000046`; accession: `0000950170-24-087843`).
- cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins. [MSFT-2024-10K-p000096](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000095017024087843/msft-20240630.htm) (chunk: `000095017024087843#passage-000096`; accession: `0000950170-24-087843`).
- We continue to identify and evaluate opportunities to expand our datacenter locations and increase our server capacity to meet the evolving needs of our customers, particularly given the growing demand for AI services. [MSFT-2024-10K-p000096](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000095017024087843/msft-20240630.htm) (chunk: `000095017024087843#passage-000096`; accession: `0000950170-24-087843`).
- Excluding the impact of the change in accounting estimate, Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage increased slightly driven by improvements in Azure and Office 365 Commercial, inclusive of scaling our AI infrastructure, offset in part by sales mix shift to Azure. [MSFT-2024-10K-p000102](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000095017024087843/msft-20240630.htm) (chunk: `000095017024087843#passage-000102`; accession: `0000950170-24-087843`).
- Our Microsoft Cloud revenue, which includes Azure and other cloud services, Office 365 Commercial, the commercial portion of LinkedIn, Dynamics 365, and other commercial cloud properties, was $ 137.4 billion, $ 111.6 billion, and $ 91.4 billion in fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively. [MSFT-2024-10K-p000186](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000095017024087843/msft-20240630.htm) (chunk: `000095017024087843#passage-000186`; accession: `0000950170-24-087843`).

Evidence gaps:
- Subquery 1 has no evidence meeting threshold after 2 retries.
